This game is a mixed bag: Looting, leveling and progressing is fun for a while. The controls are decent, the world is interesting in the beginning, and the boss fights are challenging but not overly hard.

However, it gets quite samey after 15 to 20 hours. I'm now at the point where I wish the game was over. The enemy variety feels limited, the areas repeat, and the combat against mobs is repetitive.

The game was good for scratching my souls-like itch for a while. It might do yours as well, but probably not for long. Get it at a discount and enjoy the good times!

I saw the trailer on YouTube and thought it looked really cool. I was disappointed to find out it was just a short little student project and not a full game. The game looks pretty good and the combat took a bit to get used to. Not in a bad way and once I got the hang of it I think it feels good. If it was a full game I’d love to see what kind of other moves you could get. I really like the idea of healing by stealing the melting wax of the enemies. No UI, the health is how tall the candle is. It ended right as I was really getting into it. 

I tried 3 or 4 times to get the beat under 10 minutes achievement and kept being a tiny bit too slow. I turned on God Mode and it still worked so you can cheat to get it if you want.

It's a pretty neat game. I enjoyed this play through, but I doubt I'll play it again, just for the last achievements, though. Time will tell. Other than that, the game was very enjoyable. Some of the fights can seem a little repetitive. There are some genuinely funny moments (like with the echo, lol) and it made me want to rewatch the show now.

I hate giving bad reviews over performance, but despite trying everything, UE5 won this round. The constant microstutters and traversal stutter are a total dealbreaker for me. Played on 360 back in 2014, still a banger. Art style hasn't gone out of date, mechanics still feel fun and fresh, and I still find something new every playthrough that I hadn't seen before.

There's very few reasons to not get this game;
- You're not a fan of violence.
- You're not a fan of stealth (though that's not a necessity of the game).
-  You HATE rats.
There's otherwise very few reasons most any gamer couldn't pick this up and enjoy it.

Max Payne inspired shooter game

Suit For Hire is a top down/third person shooter were you go through levels and try to obtain a high rank based on your accuracy, less deaths, kills and doing it as fast as possible.

Gameplay is fun while a bit janky sometimes with the animations but it's not that game breaking thankfully. Good music, great levels and a variety of enemies to fight.

Criticism for SFH are the two bosses who are annoying, the Caribbean's last three levels are disappointing training stages, the arena spawns are irritating so that you get surrounded pretty easily and sometimes when I use the deadeye revolver and do the execute on a enemy after stunning it my chamber didn't reload.

That's about it. Suit For Hire is pretty fun once you get a hang of the controls and mechanics.

Didn't finish it. Watched it on Youtube. 
Positive: act 1 (mother's death, deep emotional resonance), worldbuilding, aesthetics. 
Negative: 
- too many topics/elements but only surface level exploration (politics, environmentalist, religion, AI etc.)
- the plot scattered around loosely. never a fan of multiple protagonists gameplay/narrative in games. 
- trying too hard to be cool. 
- Characters interesting at first fall flat very quickly. 
- cringy humour.

in summary, everything about the mother-daughter relations is very well-written and emotionally touching. everything about the world, other characters fell flat and serves merely as flavours. It feels like a cake with too much icing on top and it never fills your stomach. you ended wanting something more.

I really enjoy this game.  The fact that it's also a dynamic "screen saver" is really fun as well.  I love leaving it just playing on idle while I do other things, either on my main monitor or on my second monitor while I'm working.  It's not a complicated game, just a lovely easy flowing progression.
If anything I just wish it had some kind of lo-fi radio in the boat that you could switch on for mood music.  I can have another program running for that, but it would be cool to have it integrated into the game as well.
Either way, I really enjoyed (and continue to enjoy) this game.  Looking forward to their next projects like Eastern Winds and the hunting version (Wild n Chill) I saw for down the line.

Best described as all style, no substance.

I read through three story synopses and even they weren't entirely sure what the story is. I was just playing a game for the sake of it. I liked Overseer, he was funny, and the final boss is beyond obvious.
Combat is alright. Its a bit floaty for my liking and the guns felt a bit numb. There wasn't a lot of weight behind them except for the Handcannon and the Zenit.
Music didn't stand out but the world design reminded me of Neon Genesis Evangelion which I love that world.
Its fine overall. Better gunplay and story is found in Doom Eternal and Ultrakill.
I almost wonder if there was more planned for the story because the potential is there, they just don't do much with it and if they did, it was not clear what was going on.
